title: Adaptive slew throttling and graceful degrade runbook for intermittent 5xx waves
creator: Jordan Reyes
description:
Summary: During a multi-tenant customer incident on 2025-02-09 we observed repeating short-lived waves of 5xx responses and long tail timeouts across hosted inference endpoints. Symptoms include proxy queue growth, rapid KV cache churn, backend kernel scheduling stalls, and aggressive client retry amplification. Multiple customers escalated due to transient failures and increased latency.

Root cause hypothesis: a combination of (1) tenant-burst traffic patterns that exceed expected concurrent token rates, (2) edge routing that fanouts requests to multiple backend hosts without admission control, (3) KV cache eviction thrash when new sequence prefixes arrive in tight loops, and (4) backend GPU kernel queuing which amplifies latency into timeouts and 5xx errors. The interplay causes client SDKs to retry too aggressively, creating a feedback loop.

Goal: Implement a short-term, low-risk mitigation (edge-level adaptive slew throttling + dynamic backoff & graceful degrade) and a medium-term hardening plan (kvcache smoothing, kernel backlog visibility, better SDK retry semantics). This ticket tracks the short-to-medium roadmap, runbook, customer communications, and rollout notes.

Proposed mitigation steps (short-term):
1) Edge admission control: add per-tenant dynamic leaky-bucket with refill rate modulated by observed backend error rate and queue depth. Burst allowance decays exponentially during 5xx spikes.
2) Slew throttling: apply a per-connection request-slew limiter to avoid fanout storms to backends when a tenant's request rate jumps.
3) Idempotency and dedupe: ensure idempotency tokens are honored at the edge to reject duplicate retry floods quickly.
4) Graceful degrade: route to a compatible, smaller model (or cached partial response) when backend latency exceeds threshold for N consecutive tokens.
5) SDK guidance: publish immediate guidance to customers to add exponential jitter backoff and recommended Timeouts.

Medium-term hardening (follow-up tickets): kvcache compaction policy, kernel admission control at runtime, per-host queue depth export to tracing, more conservative default SDK retry policy.

Telemetry & alerting: emit a new metric 'tenant_5xx_wave_score' (composite of error rate, queue depth, kvcache churn) and trigger paging at high severity. Add a Grafana dashboard tile with tenant heatmap and recent retry amplification indicators.

Testing & rollout: Canary edge rollout (5% of traffic) with synthetic burst tests, then 25%/50%/100% staged rollout. Rollback plan: revert edge admission config if error rate for non-impacted tenants rises or overall p95 latency increases by >10% relative to baseline.

Customer comms: draft messages for impacted customers with mitigation timeline, temporary SDK/timeout recommendations, and a commitment to a follow-up RCA.
acceptance_criteria: Edge admission control implemented and can be toggled via feature flag
Per-tenant leaky-bucket prevents repeat 5xx waves in synthetic burst tests
Canary rollout shows reduction in error amplification for impacted tenants without regressing baseline latency by >10%
Runbook documented with clear playbook steps and rollback instructions
Customer guidance and PR for SDK recommendations published
